subject: Pilot workload sizeup & streaming requirements — follow-up
messages:
From: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot kickoff recap: throughput and streaming questions

Thanks for the quick sync today — high level notes and open items below:

- Pilot scope: conversational streaming for patient intake (single-turn initial prompt + multi-turn clarification). Average prompt ~120 tokens; typical assistant response ~250 tokens.
- Concurrency: expected 40 concurrent active streams during clinic hours; operational spikes to ~120 concurrent for 10–15 minute windows during shift changes.
- Latency targets: 95th <= 350ms for first token, 99th <= 600ms end-to-end (we know streaming first-token SLAs are strict).
- Throughput: sustained ~18 QPS with streaming enabled; our back-of-envelope peak token/sec ≈ 12k when bursts hit.

Open asks for Redwood engineering: 
1) Can Dedicated capacity meet the 95/99 latency targets under sustained 18 QPS with streaming enabled? Any known trade-offs with batching for first-token latency?
2) Configuration suggestions: batching window, max batch size, KV cache settings for small-turn streams.
3) Recommended guardrails: circuit-breaker policy for sustained token/sec above X, and a fallback policy (model variant or region) if tail latency degrades.

I've attached the pilot workload snapshot CSV (per-call sample, peak histograms). Happy to clarify numbers if helpful.

Thanks — Morgan

--
Morgan Lee
Sr. Lead Product Manager, Acme Health
morgan.lee@acmehealth.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 16:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff recap: throughput and streaming questions

Morgan — thanks for the clear notes and for sharing the CSV. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps: 

Summary takeaways:
- Numbers look reasonable and align with similar healthcare intake pilots we've run. The sustained 18 QPS with average ~370 tokens per request (prompt+response) gives a sustained token rate ~6.7k tokens/sec; that matches your CSV medians, peak samples in the file drive the 12k estimate.
- Streaming first-token latency target is the tighter constraint (95th <= 350ms). Batching helps cost but can hurt first-token latency if windows are long.

Immediate asks we will action:
1) Marissa will run a Dedicated-capacity micro-sim (replicates 18 QPS sustained + configured 120-concurrency 15-min spike pattern) to validate 95/99 latency for first token and end-to-end. Expect a short report with tail percentiles.
2) Recs on batching: propose max batching window 10ms for streaming entry points, with an adaptive increase during low-traffic periods. We'll surface the recommended max batch size and effect on latency in the report.
3) Guardrail proposal: automatic circuit-break to degrade to a lower-cost model-variant if sustained token/sec > 10k for longer than 2 minutes, with gradual rollback once below threshold.

Can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up tomorrow to review Marissa's micro-sim results? Proposed times: 09:30 or 11:00 PST.

I'll attach our initial streaming SLO matrix and a short checklist.

Best,
Jasmine
Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 18:32:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff recap: throughput and streaming questions — micro-sim plan

Adding the micro-sim plan and preliminary numbers so we have a working frame for tomorrow's check-in. I'll attach raw run artifacts to the Drive link after the run.

Micro-sim parameters:
- Baseline: 18 QPS sustained; per-request token = 370 tokens (120 prompt + 250 response)
- Concurrency model: 40 steady concurrent streams, modeled as long-lived (keep-alive) sessions; spike window: +80 concurrent for 15 minutes (total 120)
- Burst model: spike shape = 10x short crest (10–15s) within the 15-min window to capture momentary surges

Preliminary throughput math (for clarity):
- Sustained tokens/sec = 18 QPS * 370 tokens ~= 6,660 tokens/sec
- Peak tokens/sec (from sample peaks) up to ~12,000 tokens/sec (matches Morgan's observation)

Initial sim expectations and config recs:
- Dedicated profile: 2 smaller inference shards (horizontal) with adaptive batching; aim for average first-token latency < 250ms at sustained load, tail (99th) under 600ms with spikes handled by autoscale/burst policy.
- Batching: streaming entrypoint uses adaptive max window of 5–15ms, max batch size tuned to keep first-token latency target.
- KV caching: small-turn exchanges benefit from per-session KV reuse — recommend session pinning for the 40 steady streams to reduce token work.
- Circuit-break thresholds: trigger when sustained token/sec > 10k for 2 minutes; fallback to cheaper model-variant and route new sessions to the variant while draining existing sessions.

Next steps / deliverables:
- Run micro-sim tonight, upload 95/99th percentiles and QPS vs token/sec charts to Drive (link below).
- Review results with Acme tomorrow, decide on Dedicated commit size for the pilot (we'll show cost tradeoffs).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aB2c3SAMPLE

Marissa
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff recap: throughput and streaming questions

Thanks — that plan looks solid. 09:30 PST tomorrow works for our team. Two quick clarifications before the run: 
1) For the circuit-break threshold, is the 10k tokens/sec a hard limit only for new sessions, or will existing sessions be forcibly downgraded mid-dialog? We prefer new-session routing to fallback and graceful draining of active sessions.
2) Can you include a short column in the report mapping expected incremental cost for 10k->12k tokens/sec sustained (delta per hour)? We'll use that to align finance/approvals.

If you can confirm those two items in the run notes, we can lock the 09:30 slot and invite engineering.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Morgan
